messages:
alex_dev: Heads-up: onboarding sample-app hitting weird auth/retry failures only when built with Vite + esbuild target=es2022 and run in the Edge runtime. Works fine locally with node.

maria_types: Oof. Repro steps?

alex_dev: Steps I used: clone repo, npm i, cd sample-app/examples/edge-auth, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, then build with `vite build` (esbuild target=es2022). Deploy to local edge runtime (wrangler dev / edge runtime shim). Calls to /api/generate intermittently 401 then 429 on retry.

sam_bundler: Can you paste a minimal request/headers log?

alex_dev: Sure — after build I see this in the edge logs: ```
Request POST /api/generate
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

Response 401 
Body: {"error":"invalid_token"} 
Then a retry from client lib -> 429 rate_limited
```

katie_oncall: Does the outgoing Authorization header actually get sent on the retry? Might be stripped by the bundler polyfill for fetch?

maria_types: Also check ESM/CJS interop. We're re-exporting a default from the SDK in sample-app `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; export default Redwood;` Vite + esbuild sometimes rewrites default -> `module.exports.default` shim which the edge runtime's small fetch polyfill doesn't preserve across serialization?

alex_dev: I tried changing import to `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` and then `Redwood.default.createClient(...)` — still flaky.

sam_bundler: Reproduced locally. Looks like when the SDK uses `globalThis.fetch = ...` polyfill during init, esbuild moves that into a separate chunk and the edge loader executes init twice (chunk ordering) so the token cache is empty on first request. Patch idea: avoid side-effectful top-level fetch assignment, initialize lazily.

maria_types: Also noticed TypeScript typing mismatch: the edge sample-app uses `RequestInit` augmentation from node types and the bundler strips `headers` type narrowing -> `HeadersInit | undefined` leading to accidental omission of Authorization header when headers computed via conditional spread. Example: ```ts
const headers = { ...(token && { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }), 'content-type': 'application/json' }
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers })
```
If token is falsy at build-time (due to chunking timing), header key removed.

katie_oncall: Workarounds? I can patch sample-app to always set Authorization: token || '' to ensure header exists, but that's gross.

sam_bundler: For a proper fix we should: 1) make SDK init idempotent/lazy so no top-level fetch assignment; 2) update docs with bundler caveats (vite/esbuild chunking) and provide explicit example using `new URL('.', import.meta.url)` or single-entry bundling; 3) add an integration test building with Vite target es2022 + edge shim.

alex_dev: I'll open a PR with a minimal repro repo (edge-auth-vite-repro) and a failing CI job that builds with `vite build --ssr` + wrangler dev shim. Also adding a README with quick triage steps.

maria_types: I'll propose a typesafe helper in the SDK: `buildAuthHeaders(token?: string) : Record<string,string>` that always returns the header key (possibly empty) so bundlers won't drop it.

ci-bot: CI job queued: reproducer/edge-auth-vite-repro - build@linux (this message autogenerated) :gear:

katie_oncall: Thanks — big win if we can avoid customer issues. Also add a blurb in onboarding docs: "If you use Vite + Edge runtime, prefer lazy init and explicit auth header construction."

alex_dev: Will do. TL;DR: Vite/esbuild chunk ordering + top-level side effects + header-spread pattern -> intermittent missing Authorization -> 401 -> retries -> 429. Repro repo coming.
